sources.redactions: Only the fresh access-key secret is redacted. CloudTrail account-wide event results retain only events for the exact owned log groups or role ARNs. Initial read-only Logs discovery also matched the parallel external fixture prefix after a shared eval namespace collision; unrelated stream/event reads and the derived logs projection are excluded. Exact resource ARNs, input bodies, receipts and raw feedback message strings are unchanged.

limitations: A shared eval kernel initially reused the parallel external capture prefix. Resource ownership was immediately partitioned by exact ARN; subsequent capture used an isolated subprocess. Only this fixture owns the unsuffixed function/topic, -none topic, -sqs/-receipts queues, -feedback/-wrong-trust/-lambda roles, and -config user. Parallel external resources were never mutated during managed cleanup.

SUCCESS means endpoint API acceptance, not customer execution success. This capture independently observed actual Python Lambda execution through SQS receipts; lambdaRequestId equals context.aws_request_id for correlated successful publications.
Only sample rates 0 and 100 were exercised for delivery. Fractional/intermediate sampling distributions and native UUID stream/shard allocation are not established.

Early InvalidClientTokenId and repeated role/key-policy errors are retained as propagation observations, not IAM conclusions. Identity and trust conclusions use subsequent successful controls and observed denial after policy/trust reversal.

Feedback log ingestion was delayed after endpoint delivery. Native log-event timestamps/ingestionTime are retained independently from notification timestamps and dwellTimeMs; no equivalence is assumed.

No durable logging retry or replay guarantee is inferred from bounded observation. The denied logging policy remained in force across the recorded publish, actual target receipts, and later Logs read; restoration then produced a distinct publication and later log reads.

Managed endpoint retry exhaustion over the documented multi-day retry policy was not attempted. Captured target failures are permanent authorization outcomes; no receipt for that SNS message was observed.
Management event history is eventually consistent and incomplete for data events; captured management identities are evidence only for their actual records, not proof of every PutLogEvents call.
